mainTopic: Payments that require real coins, and what a בכור may be redeemed with (רבי vs. the רבנן)
overview: This amud opens with the end of a story about חנן בישא. He owed half a זוז for a slap, but had only a damaged coin, so he slapped the man again and handed it over. The גמרא then explains why the משנה lists the payments of the אונס and the מוציא שם רע in the שקל הקודש: the Torah does not say 'שקלים' for them, so the משנה teaches that these cases are learned from one another. A ברייתא adds that שקלים, מעשר שני and the ראיון money must all be paid in real coins, and the גמרא gives a source for each. A new משנה rules that a בכור may not be redeemed with slaves, שטרות, land or הקדשות. It adds that a written IOU does not redeem the son, and that lost פדיון money must be paid again. The גמרא explains that רבי allows everything except שטרות, because he reads the פסוק as ריבוי ומיעוט. The רבנן read it as כלל ופרט וכלל, which excludes land, slaves and שטרות. רבינא challenges רבי's method from the case of the מרצע. מרימר answers that a verse with two general terms first follows תנא דבי רבי ישמעאל, while the רבנן follow the rule of מערבא. The amud ends with the גמרא asking why the משנה needs to exclude הקדשות, and the answer continues on the next amud.

steps.title: End of the story: the damaged coin and the second slap
steps.stepSummary: חנן בישא owed half a זוז for a slap. He had only a damaged, unusable זוז, so he slapped the man again and handed over the whole זוז.
steps.simpleTranslation: He had a damaged זוז with him that was not accepted as currency. So he slapped him another time and gave it to him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a story that started on the previous daf. חנן בישא was ordered to pay half a זוז for slapping someone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The fine for the slap was only half a זוז, and his coin was damaged and would not be accepted, so he could not pay. Instead of finding change, he slapped the man again so that he would owe a full זוז and could hand over the bad coin. The story shows how small the fine was, and it also shows the wickedness of חנן.

keyTerms.meaning: A זוז (דינר), a silver coin
Damaged or worn down
That does not 'go out', meaning it is not accepted in circulation
He slapped him (literally, 'struck' him)

steps.confusionAlert: This line is the end of a story that began earlier. Do not look for a question or an answer inside it. It is only the finale of the narrative.

phrases.english: He had a damaged zuz with him
phrases.notes: The subject is חנן בישא from the earlier part of the story.

phrases.english: which was not accepted in circulation;
phrases.notes: The victim would not accept it.

phrases.english: he struck him another time
phrases.notes: Now he owes a second half זוז.

phrases.english: and gave it to him.
phrases.notes: The full damaged זוז covers both slaps.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes a story begun on the previous amud.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Narrative ending: the man had a bad coin worth one זוז, so he caused a second half-זוז liability and paid the full זוז.

steps.title: The גמרא quotes the משנה about slave, rapist and seducer payments
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the משנה. The משנה lists 30 for an עבד and 50 for an אונס and a מפתה, all paid in the שקל הקודש.
steps.simpleTranslation: [The משנה says:] Thirty of a slave, fifty of a rapist and of a seducer, etc.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a new line of the משנה. It is setting up a question about why this line is needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This line of the משנה lists fixed Torah payments: 30 שקלים when an ox kills an עבד, and 50 from an אונס or a מפתה. The 'וכו׳' points to the rest of the line, which includes the 100 of the מוציא שם רע and the rule that all are paid in the שקל הקודש.

keyTerms.meaning: A Canaanite slave. If an ox kills him, its owner pays 30 שקלים
One who violates a נערה; he pays 50
One who seduces a נערה; he pays 50
'Etc.', meaning the quote continues in the משנה

phrases.english: Thirty of a slave,
phrases.notes: The payment when an ox kills a slave.

phrases.aramaic: חֲמִשִּׁים שֶׁל אוֹנֵס וְשֶׁל מְפַתֶּה וְכוּ׳.
phrases.english: fifty of a rapist and of a seducer, etc.
phrases.notes: The quote continues with the מוציא שם רע and the rule of the שקל הקודש.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁלֹשִׁים שֶׁל עֶבֶד, חֲמִשִּׁים שֶׁל אוֹנֵס וְשֶׁל מְפַתֶּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new topic: back to the text of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The fixed payments of the עבד (30), the אונס and the מפתה (50), and the מוציא שם רע (100) are paid in the שקל הקודש.

steps.title: Why repeat this, since the first clause already taught it?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the משנה needs this list. The opening clause already said that these amounts are counted in the שקל הקודש.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why do I need this further statement? The earlier clause already taught it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the משנה for repeating itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier part of the משנה already stated that payments are calculated by the שקל הקודש. Spelling out the עבד, the אונס, and the מפתה again looks unnecessary. The גמרא assumes every line of a משנה must teach something new.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Why do I need this additionally?' The גמרא asks why a statement is repeated
The first or earlier clause of the משנה
He (the תנא) taught

phrases.english: Why do I need this further?
phrases.notes: This is a challenge, not a simple request for information.

phrases.english: He already taught it in the first clause!

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא תּוּ לְמָה לִי? הָא תְּנָא לֵיהּ רֵישָׁא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the line of the משנה just quoted.
steps.kashyaTarget: The repeated listing in the משנה of the עבד, the אונס, the מפתה, and the מוציא שם רע as paid in the שקל הקודש.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Redundancy: the רישא already taught the general rule of the שקל הקודש, so the list seems to add nothing.

steps.title: Needed for the rapist and defamer, whose verses do not say 'shekels'
steps.stepSummary: The list is needed for the אונס and the מוציא שם רע. The Torah writes only 'כסף' for them, not 'שקלים', so one might think they pay plain זוזים. The משנה teaches that these cases learn from each other.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was needed for the rapist and the defamer. You might have thought that since 'shekels' is not written about them, they pay just ordinary זוזים. The משנה teaches us that they are learned from one another.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. It shows that the listing teaches something the רישא did not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the עבד, the Torah explicitly says 'שקלים'. For the אונס and the מוציא שם רע, it only says 'fifty of silver' and 'a hundred of silver'. Without the משנה we might think a cheap זוז is meant. The משנה tells us these payments are derived from one another, so all of them are full שקלים.

keyTerms.meaning: A husband who falsely claims his bride was unfaithful; he pays 100
It was needed
'It would have entered your mind to say', introducing a mistaken first thought (הוה אמינא)
'It teaches us', introducing the real lesson
They are derived from one another

steps.whatToRemember: Even when the פסוק says only 'כסף', the payments of the אונס, the מפתה, and the מוציא שם רע are in full שקלים of the שקל הקודש. These cases are learned from one another.
steps.confusionAlert: A 'שקל' is worth much more than a 'זוז' (about four זוזים). The question is not about which kind of coin is used. It is about how much money is owed.

phrases.english: The rapist and the defamer were needed,
phrases.notes: These are the cases the list really comes to teach.

phrases.english: for it would have entered your mind to say:
phrases.notes: This opens the mistaken first thought.

phrases.english: since 'shekels' is not written regarding them,
phrases.notes: The פסוקים say only 'כסף' (silver).

phrases.english: say it means merely ordinary zuzim;
phrases.notes: That would be a much lower payment.

phrases.english: so it teaches us
that they are indeed derived from one another.
phrases.notes: So all of them are paid in the שקל הקודש.

steps.triggerLanguage: אוֹנֵס וּמוֹצִיא שֵׁם רַע אִיצְטְרִיךְ, סָלְקָא דַּעְתָּךְ אָמֵינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the redundancy challenge.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows the statement is necessary to block a mistaken reading (איצטריך)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the Torah does not say 'שקלים' for the אונס and the מוציא שם רע, they would pay only ordinary זוזים.
steps.terutzMaskana: These payments are derived from one another, so all of them are full שקלים of the שקל הקודש.

steps.title: The משנה's exception: except for the shekels
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next phrase of the משנה. All obligations may be paid with money or with goods of equal value, except for the מחצית השקל.
steps.simpleTranslation: [The משנה says:] Except for the shekels.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes another phrase from the משנה. It is setting up a ברייתא that adds to this list.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה rules that most monetary obligations can be paid either in coins or in goods worth the same amount. The yearly half-שקל given to the מקדש is an exception: it must be given in actual coins.

keyTerms.meaning: Except for
The yearly מחצית השקל given to the מקדש

phrases.english: Except for the shekels.
phrases.notes: This refers to the yearly half-שקל, which must be given as coins.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new phrase of the משנה; a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Obligations may be paid with money or its value, except for the מחצית השקל, which requires actual coins.

steps.title: A ברייתא adds tithe and festival-appearance money
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches a longer list of exceptions: שקלים, מעשר שני, and the money for the ראיון. All of these must be given as actual coins.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in a ברייתא: except for the shekels, and מעשר, and the ראיון.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that adds two more items to the משנה's exception.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה named only שקלים. The ברייתא adds מעשר שני, which is redeemed with real coins taken to ירושלים, and the ראיון money, which pays for the עולת ראיה on the רגלים. For all three, goods of equal value are not enough; the payment must be in coins.

keyTerms.meaning: Here, מעשר שני, which is redeemed with actual coins
Money for the עולת ראיה brought by pilgrims on the רגלים

steps.whatToRemember: There are three exceptions that must be paid in real coins: שקלים, מעשר שני, and ראיון. Every other obligation may also be paid with goods of the same value.

phrases.english: It was taught: except for the shekels,
phrases.notes: The ברייתא repeats the משנה's exception and then adds to it.

phrases.english: and tithe, and the appearance offering.
phrases.notes: These are the added items: מעשר שני and the ראיון money.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנָא: חוּץ מִן הַשְּׁקָלִים, וּמַעֲשֵׂר, וְהָרֵאָיוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Expands the משנה's exception by quoting a ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Three obligations require actual coins: שקלים, מעשר שני, and the money for ראיון.

steps.title: Source that שקלים must be real coins
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא proves from a משנה in שקלים that the half-shekel may only be exchanged for other coins, not for goods.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shekalim — as we learned: they may combine shekels and exchange them for darics (large gold coins), because of the burden of carrying them on the road.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא listed three payments that must be real coins. Now the גמרא gives a source for the first one, שקלים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה in שקלים allows travelers to exchange heavy silver שקלים for light gold coins (דרבונות). It only allows switching to other coins, never to goods of equal value. This shows that שקלים must stay in the form of real money.

keyTerms.meaning: The yearly half-shekel given to the בית המקדש
They combine or exchange (many coins into fewer)
Darics, large gold coins
The burden of carrying on the journey

phrases.english: Shekalim — as we learned in a mishna:
they combine shekels into darics (gold coins),
phrases.notes: Only an exchange into other coins is allowed, not into goods.

phrases.english: because of the burden of the journey.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a source for the first item in the ברייתא's list of exceptions.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that שקלים must be paid in actual coins
steps.raayaSupportSource: משנה שקלים: shekels may be exchanged for darics because of the burden of travel

steps.title: Source that מעשר שני must be redeemed with coins
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק 'וצרת הכסף בידך' shows that מעשר שני is redeemed only with coins that carry a stamped image.
steps.simpleTranslation: Ma'aser — as it is written: 'And bind up the money in your hand.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a source for the second exception, מעשר שני, from a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'וצרת' is read as related to 'צורה', a stamped image. So the money used to redeem מעשר שני must be a minted coin with an image on it. Goods of equal value do not work.

keyTerms.meaning: Second tithe, eaten in ירושלים or redeemed for money
And you shall bind up; read as hinting to צוּרָה (a stamped image)
As it is written (in the תורה)

phrases.english: Second tithe — as it is written:
"And bind up the money in your hand" (Deuteronomy 14:25),
phrases.notes: וצרת is read as צורה: money with an engraved form, meaning a coin.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Second source in the same list.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that מעשר שני must be redeemed with real coins

steps.title: Source that the ראיון money must be real coins
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף teaches that a person may not bring an unrefined lump of silver into the עזרה, so the ראיון money must be proper coins.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the appearance offering — רב יוסף taught: that one should not bring a lump of base metal into the Temple courtyard.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the source for the third and last exception, the ראיון. This finishes the ברייתא's list.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Bringing a lump of mixed, unrefined metal (סיגה) into the עזרה is not respectful. So the ראיון money has to be clean, minted coins and not a metal lump or goods.

keyTerms.meaning: The offering brought when 'appearing' in the בית המקדש on the רגלים
A lump of unrefined metal mixed with dross
The courtyard of the בית המקדש

steps.whatToRemember: All three exceptions (שקלים, מעשר שני, ראיון) must be paid in real coins, and each has its own source: a משנה, a פסוק, and רב יוסף's teaching.

phrases.english: And the appearance offering — Rav Yosef taught:
that one may not bring a lump of base metal to the Temple courtyard.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Final source in the list, closing the discussion of the ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that the ראיון money must be real coins
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב יוסף's ברייתא: one may not bring סיגה into the עזרה

steps.title: New משנה: what a בכור cannot be redeemed with
steps.stepSummary: A בכור may not be redeemed with slaves, promissory notes, land, or הקדש.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: One may not redeem a firstborn son with slaves, nor with documents, nor with land, nor with consecrated property.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It lists four kinds of property that cannot be used for פדיון הבן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier we learned that payments may usually be made with goods of equal value. This משנה gives four exceptions for פדיון הבן: עבדים, שטרות, קרקעות and הקדשות. The גמרא later derives the first three from the פסוק, because they are not like the five silver shekels. הקדשות are excluded for a separate reason, which the גמרא takes up at the end of the amud.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה
Redeem (here, a firstborn son)
Documents, such as promissory notes
Land
Property consecrated to the בית המקדש

steps.confusionAlert: This does not mean פדיון הבן requires actual coins. Other movable goods worth five סלעים are fine. Only these four categories are excluded.

phrases.english: Mishna:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין פּוֹדִין לֹא בַּעֲבָדִים, וְלֹא בִּשְׁטָרוֹת,
phrases.english: One may not redeem (a firstborn) with slaves, nor with promissory notes,
nor with land, nor with consecrated items.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה after the previous discussion ended.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A בכור cannot be redeemed with עבדים, שטרות, קרקעות or הקדשות.

steps.title: A written promise to pay does not redeem the son
steps.stepSummary: If the father writes the כהן a note for five סלעים, he owes the money, but his son is still not redeemed. The כהן may give the money back as a gift.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he wrote to the כהן that he owes him five סלעים, he must pay him, but his son is not redeemed. Therefore, if the כהן wants to give it back to him as a gift, he may.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה applies its 'no שטרות' rule to a real case: a father who gives the כהן a written IOU.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The note creates a real debt, so the father must pay. But a note is not money in hand, so it does not redeem the son. The משנה adds that the כהן may return the five סלעים as a gift, and the גמרא will later discuss what 'therefore' refers to.

keyTerms.meaning: Five sela coins, the amount for פדיון הבן
Redeemed
Therefore
Gift
Permitted

steps.whyThisMatters: This separates two things: owing money and completing the מצוה. The debt is real, but the פדיון has not happened.

phrases.english: If he wrote to the priest that he is obligated
to give five sela coins —

phrases.aramaic: חַיָּיב לִיתֵּן לוֹ, וּבְנוֹ אֵינוֹ פָּדוּי.
phrases.english: he is obligated to give them to him, but his son is not redeemed.
Therefore, if the priest wishes
to give it back to him as a gift — he is permitted.
phrases.notes: The גמרא will later ask what 'therefore' is connected to.

steps.triggerLanguage: כָּתַב לְכֹהֵן שֶׁהוּא חַיָּיב לִיתֵּן חֲמִשָּׁה סְלָעִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the 'no שטרות' rule to a practical case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A note creates a debt but does not redeem the son. The כהן may return the money as a gift.

steps.title: Money set aside for פדיון that got lost
steps.stepSummary: If a father sets aside the פדיון money and it gets lost, he must pay again, because the son is redeemed only once the money reaches the כהן.
steps.simpleTranslation: One who sets aside the redemption money for his son and it was lost is responsible for it, as it says: 'shall be yours' and then 'you shall surely redeem.'
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה rules that setting aside money does not finish the פדיון. If the money is lost, the father still owes it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק first says 'יהיה לך', meaning the money must belong to the כהן. Only after that does it say 'פדה תפדה'. So the פדיון takes effect only when the כהן actually receives the money, and until then any loss falls on the father.

keyTerms.meaning: One who sets aside
The redemption money for his son
Responsibility for loss
You shall surely redeem

steps.whatToRemember: פדיון הבן takes effect only when the כהן actually gets the money. A note does not do it, and money that was set aside but lost does not do it either.

phrases.english: One who designates the redemption money of his son, and it was lost —
he is responsible for it,
as it is stated: "shall be yours," and "you shall surely redeem" (Numbers 18:15).
phrases.notes: The order of the פסוק shows the money must first reach the כהן, and only then is the son redeemed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another case in the same משנה about when the פדיון actually takes effect.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A father who set aside the פדיון money and lost it must pay again, learned from 'יהיה לך' followed by 'פדה תפדה'.

steps.title: Our משנה does not follow רבי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא states that the משנה does not follow רבי. In a ברייתא, רבי rules that a בכור may be redeemed with anything except שטרות.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: Our משנה is not like רבי. A ברייתא teaches that רבי says: one may redeem a human firstborn with anything, except for documents.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that the משנה we just learned disagrees with רבי. It brings a ברייתא where רבי allows almost anything to be used for פדיון הבן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה excluded slaves, שטרות, land, and הקדש. רבי excludes only שטרות, so by his view slaves and land would work. That is why the משנה must follow a different view, the רבנן.

keyTerms.meaning: Not in line with רבי (רבי יהודה הנשיא)
One may redeem with anything
A human firstborn son
Documents, such as promissory notes

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think רבי allows הקדש or other things the משנה banned for separate reasons. The only argument here is over what kinds of items can count as payment. רבי excludes only שטרות.

phrases.english: GEMARA: Our Mishnah is not in accordance with Rabbi,
as it is taught: Rabbi says:
with anything one may redeem a human firstborn,
except for documents.
phrases.notes: Promissory notes are only proof of a debt. They have no value of their own.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: It returns to the משנה's list of things that cannot be used for redemption and shows that רבי disagrees.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The משנה does not follow רבי. רבי allows redemption with anything except שטרות.

steps.title: What is רבי's reason?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where רבי gets his broad rule from.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason of רבי?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the source of רבי's view. This sets up the next step, where it explains how he reads the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי's rule is very broad, yet it still has one exception. The גמרא wants to know which reading of the פסוק gives both parts: almost everything is allowed, but שטרות are not.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason or source?
Of רבי

phrases.english: What is the reason of Rabbi?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: It asks for the source of the opinion just quoted.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which reading of the פסוק leads רבי to allow everything except שטרות.

steps.title: רבי reads the verse as include, exclude, include
steps.stepSummary: רבי reads the פסוק with the method of ריבוי ומיעוט. The first words include, the words about five silver shekels exclude, and the word תפדה includes again.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי interprets with inclusions and exclusions. "And its redemption from one month you shall redeem" is an inclusion. "According to your valuation, five silver shekels" is an exclusion. "You shall redeem" is another inclusion.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי splits the פסוק into three parts: include, exclude, include again.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words "its redemption" are open-ended, so they include anything. The words "five silver shekels" narrow it down to things like money. Then "תפדה" opens it up again.

keyTerms.meaning: He interprets a פסוק
The method of reading words as inclusions and exclusions
It included (made the group wider)
It excluded (made the group narrower)
And its redemption
According to your valuation

phrases.english: He interprets with inclusions and exclusions:
"And its redemption from one month you shall redeem" — it included;
"According to your valuation, five silver shekels" — it excluded;
"You shall redeem" — it included.
phrases.notes: במדבר יח:טז

steps.relationToPreviousStep: It answers the question by giving רבי's reading method.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי uses ריבוי ומיעוט and reads the פסוק as include, exclude, include.

steps.title: Include-exclude-include brings in everything except notes
steps.stepSummary: The rule of ריבה ומיעט וריבה is that almost everything is included. The only thing left out is what is least like money, which is שטרות.
steps.simpleTranslation: When it included, then excluded, then included, it included everything. What did it include? Everything. What did it exclude? Documents.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא applies the rule of the method to finish explaining רבי's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With ריבה ומיעט וריבה, the two inclusions outweigh the one exclusion. So almost everything is allowed, even slaves and land. The exclusion still removes something: שטרות, because a note has no value of its own, so it is the least like a silver coin.

keyTerms.meaning: An inclusion, then an exclusion, then another inclusion
It included everything
All things

steps.whatToRemember: רבי reads the פסוק as ריבה ומיעט וריבה. So everything can be used to redeem a בכור except שטרות.

phrases.english: It included, excluded, and included — it included everything.
What did it include? It included all things;
and what did it exclude? It excluded documents.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: It applies the method's rule to the three parts found in the previous step.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The two inclusions bring in everything. The one exclusion removes only שטרות.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי's rule, everything except שטרות, comes from reading the פסוק as ריבה ומיעט וריבה.

steps.title: The רבנן read the verse as general, specific, general
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן read the same פסוק with the method of כלל ופרט. The first words are a general statement, the five silver shekels are a specific detail, and תפדה is a general statement again.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן interpret with general and specific. "And its redemption from one month" is a general statement. "According to your valuation, five silver shekels" is a specific detail. "You shall redeem" goes back and makes a general statement.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins to explain the רבנן, whose view the משנה follows. This step sets up their reading, and the next step will show what it leads to.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sides use the same three parts of the פסוק, but they read them with different methods. A כלל ופרט וכלל reading limits things to items like the detail, which means movable items with value of their own, like coins. That is why the רבנן exclude slaves and land, not just שטרות.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sages who disagree with רבי
The method of reading words as general and specific
It made a general statement
It gave a specific detail
It went back and made a general statement again

steps.confusionAlert: ריבוי ומיעוט and כלל ופרט look the same on the surface, since both split the פסוק into three parts. But they give very different results. ריבוי ומיעוט includes almost everything. כלל ופרט וכלל includes only things similar to the detail.

phrases.english: And the Rabbis interpret with general and specific:
"And its redemption from one month" — a general statement;
"According to your valuation, five silver shekels" — a specific detail;
"You shall redeem" — it went back and made a general statement.
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the word in round brackets, (פדה).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After explaining רבי, the גמרא gives the opposing reading of the same פסוק, which is the source for the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The רבנן read the פסוק as כלל ופרט וכלל. Their conclusion is finished in the next part of the גמרא.

steps.title: The rule of a general statement, a detail, and a general statement, applied to redemption
steps.stepSummary: Under כלל ופרט וכלל, we only include things similar to the detail. The detail, silver shekels, is movable and is itself money, so anything like that may be used.
steps.simpleTranslation: When there is a general statement, then a detail, then a general statement, you may only include things similar to the detail. The detail here is clearly something movable whose body itself is money. So too, anything that is movable and whose body itself is money may be used.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains what the רבנן's method of כלל ופרט וכלל actually produces. Only things similar to the five silver shekels can be used to redeem a בכור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With ריבה ומיעט וריבה (רבי's method), almost everything is included. With כלל ופרט וכלל (the רבנן's method), we only include things that share the key features of the detail. The גמרא names two features of silver coins: they are movable, and they are money in their very body.

keyTerms.term: אִי אַתָּה דָן אֶלָּא כְּעֵין הַפְּרָט
keyTerms.meaning: You may only include things similar to the detail
Clearly stated, explicit
Something movable
Its body itself is money (it has real value of its own)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two methods. ריבה ומיעט וריבה includes almost everything. כלל ופרט וכלל includes only things like the detail. The same פסוק gives a wider or narrower result depending on which method you use.

phrases.english: A general statement, a detail, and a general statement

phrases.aramaic: אִי אַתָּה דָן אֶלָּא כְּעֵין הַפְּרָט.
phrases.english: you may only include things similar to the detail.
Just as the detail is clearly
something movable whose body itself is money,

phrases.aramaic: אַף כׇּל דָּבָר הַמִּטַּלְטֵל וְגוּפוֹ מָמוֹן.
phrases.english: so too, anything movable whose body itself is money.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּלָל וּפְרָט וּכְלָל, אִי אַתָּה דָן אֶלָּא כְּעֵין הַפְּרָט
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the רבנן's derivation that began in step 17 by applying the rule of כלל ופרט וכלל.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Only items that are movable and intrinsically valuable may be used to redeem a בכור.

steps.title: What the רבנן exclude: land, slaves, and documents
steps.stepSummary: Land is excluded because it is not movable. Slaves are excluded because the Torah compares them to land. שטרות are excluded because, although movable, they are not money in themselves.
steps.simpleTranslation: Land is excluded, because it is not movable. Slaves are excluded, because they are compared to land. Documents are excluded, because even though they are movable, their body is not money.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא lists the three things that fail the רבנן's test and so cannot be used to redeem a בכור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each exclusion fails one of the two features from step 18. Land and slaves fail the 'movable' feature, since slaves count like land in halacha. שטרות are movable but fail the 'body is money' feature, because a paper is only proof of a debt. So the רבנן exclude three things, while רבי excluded only שטרות.

keyTerms.meaning: Land, real estate
(Canaanite) slaves
Were compared, linked by the Torah (a היקש)

steps.whatToRemember: רבי (ריבה ומיעט וריבה) excludes only שטרות. The רבנן (כלל ופרט וכלל) exclude land, slaves, and שטרות. The disagreement comes from the two different methods of reading the same פסוק.

phrases.english: Land is excluded, because it is not movable;
slaves are excluded, because they are compared to land;
documents are excluded,
because even though they are movable,
their body itself is not money.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the test from step 18 to name what is left out.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Land, slaves, and שטרות cannot be used to redeem a בכור according to the רבנן.

steps.title: רבינא asks: doesn't רבי use general statements and details?
steps.stepSummary: רבינא challenges מרימר. Elsewhere, regarding the מרצע, רבי reads with כללי ופרטי, not ריבויי ומיעוטי.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said to מרימר: Does רבי really read פסוקים with inclusions and exclusions? But רבי reads with general statements and details in the case of the awl!
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא attacks the explanation from step 15. In another place, רבי seems to use the opposite method.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 15 said that רבי reads the פסוק of פדיון בכור with ריבוי ומיעוט. רבינא claims that in the case of the מרצע, רבי uses כלל ופרט, the רבנן's method. If רבי consistently uses כללי ופרטי, then the explanation of his view here falls apart.

keyTerms.meaning: Expounds, derives from a פסוק
An awl, used to pierce the ear of an עבד עברי who wants to stay

phrases.english: Ravina said to Mareimar:
And does Rabbi expound with inclusions and exclusions?

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא רַבִּי כְּלָלֵי וּפְרָטֵי דָּרֵישׁ בְּמַרְצֵעַ!
phrases.english: But Rabbi expounds with general statements and details regarding the awl!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי, רִיבּוּיֵי וּמִיעוּטֵי דָּרֵישׁ? וְהָא רַבִּי כְּלָלֵי וּפְרָטֵי דָּרֵישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the method attributed to רבי in steps 15 and 16.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that רבי reads the פסוק of פדיון בכור with ריבוי ומיעוט.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי is known to use כללי ופרטי in the case of the מרצע, so it is inconsistent to say he uses ריבויי ומיעוטי here.

steps.title: The baraita about the awl
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא records a מחלוקת. רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה includes any handheld object for piercing. רבי includes only metal objects, like the awl.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: 'Awl.' I only know an awl. From where do I include a palm thorn, a thorn, a needle, a drill, and a stylus? The פסוק says 'and you shall take,' to include anything that can be taken by hand. These are the words of רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה. רבי says: 'Awl.' Just as an awl is special in being made of metal, so too anything made of metal.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the source for רבינא's claim. It is a ברייתא about which tools may be used to pierce the slave's ear.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה includes almost anything held in the hand, which is a very broad result. רבי includes only metal items like the awl, which is the narrow 'similar to the detail' pattern. That narrow pattern is typical of כלל ופרט.

keyTerms.meaning: A thorn of a palm tree
A thorn
A drill or gimlet
A stylus for writing
'And you shall take' (the inclusive word in the פסוק)
Metal

phrases.english: As it was taught: 'Awl'
I only know an awl;
from where do we include a palm thorn and a thorn,
and a needle, a drill, and a stylus?
The verse says: 'And you shall take'
to include anything that can be taken by hand;
these are the words of Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Yehuda.
Rabbi says: 'Awl'
just as an awl is special in being made of metal,
so too anything made of metal.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the ברייתא that רבינא's challenge is based on.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא about the מרצע, where רבי limits the tools to metal ones.

steps.title: The earlier analysis: רבי uses general statements and details
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא recalls its earlier explanation of that מחלוקת. רבי uses כללי ופרטי, and רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה uses ריבויי ומיעוטי.
steps.simpleTranslation: And we said: About what do they disagree? רבי expounds with general statements and details, and רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה expounds with inclusions and exclusions.
steps.whatsHappening: This finishes רבינא's challenge. The גמרא itself (in קידושין) explained that the awl מחלוקת is about which method each תנא uses, and it said רבי uses כללי ופרטי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This makes the contradiction sharp. There, רבי is the one who uses כללי ופרטי. Here, we said he uses ריבויי ומיעוטי. The next step answers it.

keyTerms.meaning: And we said (citing an earlier analysis of the גמרא)
About what do they disagree?

phrases.english: And we said: About what do they disagree?
Rabbi expounds with general statements and details,

phrases.aramaic: ורבי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה דָּרֵישׁ רִיבּוּיֵי וּמִיעוּטֵי.
phrases.english: and Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Yehuda expounds with inclusions and exclusions.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the proof from the ברייתא by citing the גמרא's own analysis of it.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי's method is כללי ופרטי.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The established analysis of the מרצע מחלוקת.

steps.title: רבי Usually Uses Generalizations and Details, but Not Here
steps.stepSummary: מרימר admits that רבי usually reads verses with כללי ופרטי. In this verse, though, he follows the method of תנא דבי רבי ישמעאל.
steps.simpleTranslation: Yes, in general רבי expounds verses with generalizations and details. Here, though, he follows what the school of רבי ישמעאל taught.
steps.whatsHappening: מרימר answers רבינא's challenge. He agrees that רבי normally uses כללי ופרטי, but says this verse is a special case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבינא had pointed out that רבי uses כללי ופרטי for the מרצע, so why use ריבויי ומיעוטי for פדיון בכור? מרימר does not deny רבי's usual method. He says this verse has a special word order that calls for a different reading, and he will explain it in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Yes, indeed. This concedes the point being raised.
In general, elsewhere
But here, in this case
A teaching from the study hall of רבי ישמעאל

phrases.english: Yes, in general (elsewhere),
Rabbi expounds using generalizations and details,
but here, it is like what the school of Rabbi Yishmael taught.
phrases.notes: The special reason is spelled out in the next step.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִין בְּעָלְמָא רַבִּי כְּלָלֵי וּפְרָטֵי דָּרֵישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of רבינא raised in steps 20 to 22.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction: a general method versus a special verse structure
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since רבי uses כללי ופרטי for the מרצע, he should use it everywhere, including פדיון בכור.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי usually uses כללי ופרטי. A verse with two general terms first and the detail afterward is read as ריבוי ומיעוט.

steps.title: The Fish Verse: 'In the Water' Written Twice
steps.stepSummary: תנא דבי רבי ישמעאל teaches that when במים appears twice before the details, the verse is read as ריבה ומיעט, not as כלל ופרט.
steps.simpleTranslation: The school of רבי ישמעאל taught: 'in the water, in the water' appears two times. This is not a generalization and a detail. Rather, the verse amplified and then restricted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the source that מרימר relied on. It is a teaching about the verse on kosher fish, where the general term 'in the water' comes twice before the details.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When two general terms come first and the detail comes after, תנא דבי רבי ישמעאל says the normal כלל ופרט reading does not apply. Instead the verse is read as ריבוי ומיעוט. The פדיון בכור verse has the same shape: two general terms first, then the detail of 'כסף חמשת שקלים'. So רבי reads it as ריבוי ומיעוט.

keyTerms.meaning: In the water. This is the general term in the verse about kosher fish (ויקרא יא:ט).
Two times
It amplified and restricted. This means the verse is read with the ריבוי ומיעוט method.
A generalization followed by a detail

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רבי switched methods for no reason. The word order of the verse decides the method: two general terms followed by a detail are read as ריבוי ומיעוט.

phrases.english: As the school of Rabbi Yishmael taught:
"in the water," "in the water," two times,
phrases.notes: Then come the details: 'in the seas and in the streams'.

phrases.english: this is not a generalization and a detail,
rather, it amplified and restricted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Quotes the source that step 23 relied on.
steps.raayaObject: רבי's use of ריבוי ומיעוט in the פדיון בכור verse
steps.raayaSupportSource: תנא דבי רבי ישמעאל on the fish verse (במים written twice)
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the order of general and specific words in a verse can change which method of reading is used.

steps.title: The רבנן Follow the Rule From ארץ ישראל
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן follow the rule taught in מערבא: when two general terms are next to each other, place the detail between them and read the verse as כלל ופרט.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the רבנן say: it is as we say in the West (ארץ ישראל). Wherever you find two general terms right next to each other, put the detail between them and judge them as a generalization and a detail.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the רבנן still read this verse as כלל ופרט וכלל. They rely on a different rule taught in ארץ ישראל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן do not accept that two general terms first means ריבוי ומיעוט. Instead, they mentally move the detail into the middle, so the verse reads as general, then detail, then general. That gives the כלל ופרט וכלל reading from steps 18 and 19: only movable things that are themselves money may be used.

keyTerms.meaning: The West, meaning ארץ ישראל
Two general terms
Placed right next to each other
Place the detail between them
And judge (expound) them

steps.whatToRemember: רבי reads two general terms followed by a detail as ריבוי ומיעוט, following תנא דבי רבי ישמעאל. The רבנן move the detail into the middle and read it as כלל ופרט, following מערבא. That is the root of their disagreement about what may be used for פדיון בכור.

phrases.english: And the Rabbis say:
as we say in the West (Eretz Yisrael),
wherever you find
two generalizations juxtaposed to each other,
place the detail between them,
and expound them as a generalization and a detail.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After explaining רבי, the גמרא now explains the opposing reading of the רבנן.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What is the basis for the רבנן reading the verse as כלל ופרט?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: They follow the rule of מערבא: place the detail between the two general terms.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה: Not With Consecrated Items
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next clause of the משנה: a בכור may not be redeemed with הקדשות.
steps.simpleTranslation: And not with consecrated items.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic by quoting a line from the משנה. This line sets up the question that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says a firstborn son may not be redeemed using items that were consecrated to the Temple. The גמרא quotes this line so it can analyze it.

keyTerms.meaning: Consecrated items that belong to the Temple

phrases.english: And not with consecrated items.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves away from the כלל ופרט discussion to a new clause of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A בכור may not be redeemed with הקדשות.

steps.title: Isn't That Obvious?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the משנה needs to say this. Consecrated items do not belong to the person, so of course he cannot use them.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is obvious! They are not his!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the משנה's line as unnecessary.
steps.deeperAnalysis: To redeem a בכור, a person must give something of his own. Consecrated items belong to the Temple, not to him, so it seems obvious that he cannot use them. The גמרא asks what new point the משנה is teaching.

keyTerms.meaning: It is obvious. Why would this need to be said?
They are not his

phrases.english: It is obvious!
They are not his!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the משנה clause quoted in step 26.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Consecrated property does not belong to the person, so excluding it seems unnecessary.

steps.title: The Answer Begins: 'Say...'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא starts its answer with 'אימא', meaning 'say', and suggests a different reading of the משנה. The answer continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say:
steps.whatsHappening: This one word sets up the next move. The גמרא is about to re-read the משנה so that its line teaches something new.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'אימא' tells us the גמרא will reinterpret the משנה's words to avoid the 'obvious' problem. The actual content of the answer comes on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: Say, read it as. This introduces a new reading.

phrases.english: Say:
phrases.notes: The answer continues on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the answer to the קשיא in step 27.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-reading the wording of the משנה (completed on the next amud)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Read plainly, the clause 'ולא בהקדשות' seems only to say that a person cannot redeem with items that are not his, which is obvious. The answer, which continues on the next amud, re-reads the clause so that it teaches something new.
